correctness.rationale: The graph distance is ceil(s/2) at cyclic separation s. For M=floor(n/2), moving two steps toward the antipode increases distance for s≤M−2; the two top separations tie if M is even, while only M is maximal if M is odd. This proves the stated mutually maximally distant step table. A third vertex cannot strongly resolve a mutually maximally distant pair; conversely a geodesic through any given pair can be extended one end at a time until its endpoints are mutually maximally distant, and covering that endpoint pair resolves the original pair. The basis complements are therefore exactly the maximum independent sets of the auxiliary graph. In residue 2 this gives matching transversals and a cube. In residue 0 antipodal fibers have equality constraints along their chain and an opposite-side seam, so a full assignment is impossible; dropping one fiber leaves a path with exactly two choices, producing the listed intervals and precisely the start-index shifts ±1 as exchanges. In residues 1 and 3 the multipliers give C_n(1,3) and C_n. Allowed gaps and their total slack force one length-five or length-three gap respectively, with all other gaps two. The long gap cannot be split into two allowed gaps; removing an endpoint instead permits the two ordered splits that move the long gap. This gives precisely the exchanges ±2 on the start labels and hence an odd cycle. The argument applies from n=6 (the first 2,3,0,1 cases being 6,7,8,9); counts and diameters follow from those graphs. The uploaded checker was inspected but not executed; its finite cases are only diagnostic.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The classification requires identifying all optimum sets after the reduction. Also, any maximum-independent-set jump is a slide in the auxiliary graph, since otherwise one could add the new vertex without removal. This general move fact alone gives no exchange graph and does not imply sliding in the original input graph.

value.rationale: The graph and optimum exchange operation are natural. The result determines every optimum basis, not just the minimum size, and separates two qualitatively distinct exchange geometries, one with exponentially many solutions. The signed antipodal seam and the odd forbidden-gap pattern explain why the other residues behave differently.
